html:
SMTO-CFG-0029 — SMTO couldn't load its list of slash commands

GUID: 73480db7-4f81-4817-9469-6521743059c2
Slug: command-registration-invalid
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO stopped while starting because two of its slash commands (like /stop or /status) share a name, or one has a name it can't use. Your conversations aren't affected.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you or someone else changed SMTO's program files (for example to add or rename a slash command), undo that change, then select Start again. Every slash command and its short alias needs its own lowercase name, and an edited command list can break that rule.
  2. Otherwise, run the SMTO installer again to replace the program files, then start SMTO. The slash-command list ships with SMTO itself, so a fresh install restores a list that loads correctly.
  3. If it still stops, open Technical details and select Copy error details. The message says whether a name was used twice or contains characters SMTO can't accept.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen reaches Ready, and sending /help in a conversation lists the available commands.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who installed SMTO. Don't delete SMTO's data folder; your conversations are stored there and aren't the cause of this problem.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Server startup failed in CommandRegistry.register because a slash-command name or alias is empty, uses characters outside lowercase a-z, 0-9, _ and -, or duplicates another registered name or alias.

What this means

  • Command registration has an empty/non-lowercase/non-ASCII allowed name or duplicate name/alias within or across registrations. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Command registration has an empty/non-lowercase/non-ASCII allowed name or duplicate name/alias within or across registrations.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect plugin/build registration names and aliases against the existing registry.

How to fix it

  • Inspect CATALOG in src/agent_runtime/commands/control_plane.py and the /restart, /shutdown and /shutdownserver definitions in RestartCoordinator.definitions (src/agent_runtime/commands/restart.py) for a name or alias that is empty, not lowercase [a-z0-9_-], or collides with another entry; registration runs in register_command_routes during Server startup. Fix or revert that change (or reinstall an unmodified build), then restart the Server.
  • Correct the command registration so names and aliases are valid and unique. Reload the matching plugin/build after reviewing the change.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Every registered name/alias is unique and uses the supported lowercase character set.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
